findings.issue_text: [BUG] Both migrations 0917 and 0920 are gutted to no-ops that point at a '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py' file which is not present in this diff, so if that file does not already exist on the base branch the org saved-searches-to-views data conversion never runs at all. Every deployment that applies 0917/0920 performs no conversion and no replacement migration exists in the PR, silently dropping the data backfill this migration chain was created for.

[BUG] The four x-programs entries invoke 'sentry run consumer' with consumer names (eap-spans-subscription-results, subscription-results-eap-items, metrics-subscription-results, generic-metrics-subscription-results) that are subscription-results consumers owned by snuba, not registered sentry consumers, so the commands fail at startup. 'sentry run consumer <name>' exits with an unknown-consumer error and the tracing devservices profile never comes up, blocking the feature this config change is meant to support.

[BUG] The snuba-metrics service is declared with mode 'containerized-metrics-dev', a mode name that the snuba devservices integration does not provide (snuba ships 'containerized' and 'containerized-profiles' style modes), so devservices cannot resolve how to launch this dependency. Running 'devservices up' with the tracing profile fails to materialize snuba-metrics, breaking local setup for anyone who selects that profile.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), but _truncate_title is defined as a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration in this diff, so the call only resolves if PRCommentWorkflow inherits from CommitContextIntegration. If PRCommentWorkflow is a standalone collaborator class (it is constructed with an integration rather than subclassing it), every merged-PR comment body build raises AttributeError: type object 'PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title', breaking GitHub and GitLab PR comments for merged PRs; the GitHub/GitLab call sites route through this method so both integrations fail together.

[BUG] validate_timestamp and validate_age use truthiness checks (self.initial_data.get("age") / get("timestamp")), so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypasses the mutual-exclusion rule, and a report containing neither age nor timestamp passes validation entirely. A report with timestamp present and age=0 is accepted even though the spec says age must be absent, and a report with neither field is accepted with no ingest-time ordering information; downstream consumers indexing by report time get None/missing values for reports the W3C draft says must carry one of the two fields.

[ADVISORY] The new error-context behavior is gated only on the raw query parameter enable_error_context (default 'true') with no feature flag or options entry, and the default path now unconditionally runs a Snuba query (query_replay_instance) plus a nodestore get_multi before pagination on every GET. Every summarize-breadcrumbs request — including clients that never asked for error context — pays a new Snuba query and N nodestore reads per replay, and operators cannot turn the added load off without a code deploy or per-request client change; a slow/degraded nodestore turns a previously storage-metadata-only endpoint into one that can time out before pagination even starts.

[ADVISORY] error_ids is extracted from response[0].get("error_ids", []) after process_raw_response(fields=request.query_params.getlist("field")), so the error context is populated only when the client happens to request the error_ids field. A client that enables error context (omits enable_error_context=false) but does not pass field=error_ids in the query gets a silently empty error-events list and a summary generated without any error information — no error, no warning, just a degraded Seer summary; the contract between the two query params is undocumented in the endpoint.

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info is called per issue inside the comment-body list comprehension and wraps get_recommended_event/get_environment in a bare except Exception that downgrades every failure to an info log. Building a comment for N merged issues triggers up to N recommended-event/nodestore lookups on the PR-comment path, and any per-issue failure (nodestore outage, serialization error) is silently swallowed so comments are rendered without environment info while the underlying failure is invisible at warning/error level — the on-call signal for a systemic nodestore problem is N info-level logs.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds substantial new behavior-bearing logic (fetch_error_details nodestore fan-out, timestamp-merge ordering in gen_request_data, the enable_error_context branch) and no test-shaped file for this endpoint appears anywhere in the visible diff. The merge-ordering invariant in gen_request_data (errors interleaved with breadcrumb events by timestamp, including the tail flush) and the None-filtering in fetch_error_details are regression-prone with zero coverage; a regression would silently corrupt the Seer input prompt for replay summaries, which no existing test would catch.

[ADVISORY] Both 0917 and 0920 are converted to unconditional no-ops that defer to a 0921 migration not present in this diff, so the correctness of the data conversion for any environment that already recorded 0917/0920 as applied rests entirely on an out-of-diff file. If any deployment (self-hosted snapshot, pre-release environment) has 0917 or 0920 marked applied — i.e., the 'never run' claim is false for that environment — no replacement conversion ever executes for it and organization saved searches are permanently lost from the views migration with no backfill path in this diff; the diff provides no verification that 0921 exists or covers the owner_id__isnull=False filter that 0920 added.

[BUG] Only the null-segment-id guard in _make_recording_filenames in this diff is traceable to the PR's stated intent ('Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System'); the other ~20 files (devservices config, feedback prompt rewrite, grouping experiment removal, GitHub/GitLab PR comment templates, browser reporting serializer rewrite, preprod analytics, detector owner field, workflow engine refactors, task deadline tuning, mass frontend Flex refactors) implement work unrelated to replay bulk delete. The PR cannot be reviewed or reverted against its stated requirement: an unrelated change (e.g. the autofix default flip or the browser-reporting 422-on-any-invalid-report behavior change) ships to production hidden under a replay-delete title, and reverting the replay feature forces reverting unrelated features or cherry-picking.

[ADVISORY] DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT changes from "low" to "off" (and projectoptions/defaults.py sentry:autofix_automation_tuning default from "low" to "off") with no requirement in the PR scope traceable to it. Every project that has not explicitly set the option silently stops running automated autofix on new issues after this deploys; if this product-behavior flip was not the intent, it disables a paid AI feature fleet-wide without a changelog or feature flag, and the two constants must be kept in sync manually since they are duplicated defaults.

[ADVISORY] The collector is converted from permissive dataclass instantiation to strict DRF validation that returns 422 with error details for the entire batch when any single report fails validation, which is behavior drift untraceable to the replay-delete intent. Browsers that send a report variant not in BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES (or an age/timestamp mismatch) now get a 422 for the whole POST body, so all valid reports in the same payload are dropped and never counted; previously each report was accepted and counted individually.

[ADVISORY] Migrations 0917 and 0920 are converted to no-ops that point at a 0921 migration which is not part of this diff, so this PR guts two data migrations while deferring the replacement to an out-of-diff file. If 0921 does not land in the same release train, environments that run 0917/0920 as no-ops never convert organization saved searches to views and the backfill is silently lost; the PR title gives no hint that saved-search data migration sequencing is being changed here.

[ADVISORY] The dcg_to_slow_conditions pre-fetch, the no_slow_condition_groups logging branch, and the signature changes to get_condition_query_groups/get_groups_to_fire are performance-refactor work unrelated to replay bulk delete. A reviewer verifying the replay-delete feature must also audit a change to the delayed-workflow hot path (including the new log volume from no_slow_condition_groups on every batch containing stale DCGs), and a regression in this unrelated refactor is attributed to the replay PR in bisects.

[ADVISORY] The summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint gains Snuba replay lookup, nodestore multi-get of error events, and merge-with-breadcrumbs logic — a full feature expansion of replay AI summaries, not replay bulk delete. The default GET path of this endpoint now makes two additional remote calls (Snuba query plus nodestore get_multi) unconditionally before pagination; if this belongs to a different feature it should be its own PR, because reverting or bisecting the summarize feature is now entangled with the bulk-delete PR.

[ADVISORY] The devservices config adds a snuba-metrics service and four subscription-results consumers wired into the tracing dependency list, none of which are required by replay bulk delete or by anything else in this diff. Every developer running `sentry devserver` with the tracing mode now starts six additional containers/consumers, increasing local resource use and startup failure surface for changes this PR does not require.

[ADVISORY] A new preprod analytics event (preprod_artifact.api.assemble) and its emission are added to the assemble endpoint, untraceable to the replay-delete requirement. The analytics event is recorded before the feature flag check, so the event fires for users/organizations without the preprod-artifact-assemble feature, polluting analytics with attempts that were rejected; the change also rides in a PR whose reviewers have no context for preprod instrumentation.

[ADVISORY] The PR comment template change (bullet glyph, title truncation, environment info, removal of culprit subtitle) is unrelated product work bundled into this PR, and get_environment_info swallows all exceptions with a broad `except Exception`. Reviewers of the replay PR cannot meaningfully sign off on a change to GitHub/GitLab PR bot comment output (including the new per-issue get_recommended_event() call on the comment-rendering path), and any exception from environment lookup is silenced to info-level, hiding real breakage in comment rendering.

[BUG] A single invalid report in the batch now causes the entire POST to return 422 and discard all reports, because validation failure returns early inside the per-report loop instead of skipping the offending report. Browsers send reports as a batch; one unknown/foreign 'type' value (the browser Reporting API adds new types over time) or one malformed entry now drops every valid report in the same payload, a forward-compat regression versus the old per-report construction. An unrecognized future report type from a Chrome update will 422 whole batches until the hardcoded BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES list is updated.

[BUG] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators use truthy checks (self.initial_data.get("age")), so age=0 or timestamp=0 is treated as absent and the exclusion invariant is not enforced for zero values. A report carrying both timestamp and age=0 (or timestamp=0 and age) passes validation even though the spec forbids both being present; the promised invariant in the error message ('If timestamp is present, age must be absent') is only enforced for non-zero values.

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info is defined on CommitContextIntegration, but get_merged_pr_single_issue_template reaches into PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title and PRCommentWorkflow subclasses invoke self.get_environment_info, coupling two parallel ABC hierarchies whose inheritance relationship this diff does not establish. If PRCommentWorkflow does not also inherit CommitContextIntegration, every merged-PR comment generation raises AttributeError on self.get_environment_info (and PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title resolves only by accident of module layout); any reordering or extraction of these classes breaks comment posting on GitHub and GitLab. The base integration class referencing a sibling workflow class by name is a boundary/ownership violation that makes the next change here risky.

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info is called per issue inside get_comment_body's list comprehension, issuing issue.get_recommended_event()/get_environment() lookups (nodestore/DB hits) in an N+1 pattern over up to the comment's issue list. A PR comment referencing many issues performs one event-resolution fetch per issue inside the webhook/comment-building path, serially; latency and provider load grow linearly with issue count on every merged-PR comment.

[ADVISORY] The autofix automation default is duplicated in two hand-maintained locations (constants.py DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT and projectoptions/defaults.py register default) that must be edited in lockstep, and the value change silently flips behavior for all newly-registered projects from autofix-on to autofix-off. The next editor who changes one copy but not the other introduces a drift where projects registered before the options registry change get 'off' while code paths reading the constant expect otherwise (or vice versa); meanwhile existing orgs that never opted in see Seer autofix silently stop firing after upgrade, with no migration or feature flag gating the default flip.

[ADVISORY] The typed Literal alias BrowserReportType was replaced by a plain list of strings, weakening the discriminator from compile-checkable to runtime-only while keeping it hand-maintained in parallel with the spec. Adding a new report type is now a data edit with no type-checker signal at any usage site, and the W3C-spec comment explaining each entry was deleted, so the next contributor adding a type loses the documentation of which spec (draft vs editor's draft) carries it.

[ADVISORY] error_ids is read from response[0].get("error_ids", []) where the fields list comes from the client-controlled 'field' query params, so when the caller does not request field=error_ids the error-context feature silently produces nothing. The summarize endpoint's new error-context enrichment (snuba query plus nodestore get_multi) is dead weight unless the client happens to pass the exact field name; the response shape now encodes a contract (error_ids must be in 'field') that the endpoint neither enforces nor documents, so a client omitting it gets silently degraded summaries with no error.

[ADVISORY] The analytics.record call fires before the feature-flag check, recording preprod_artifact.api.assemble events for every organization regardless of whether the preprod-artifact-assemble feature is enabled. Analytics dashboards built on this event will count requests from orgs that cannot actually use the endpoint, inflating adoption metrics with feature-flag-blocked traffic; the event also fires for requests that subsequently fail validation.

[BUG] Migrations 0917 and 0920 were gutted to no-ops pointing at '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py', which is not added anywhere in this diff, so the org-saved-searches-to-views conversion no longer exists in any applied migration. On any deployment that applies migrations from this tree without 0921, existing organization saved searches are silently never converted to GroupSearchView rows — users' org views disappear with no data migration and no error; the intent 'convert org saved searches to views' is lost by a review iteration that replaced the migration body with a comment.

[BUG] The default for DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT (and the matching projectoption default in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py line 205) was silently flipped from 'low' to 'off', disabling automatic autofix for every new project by default. All new organizations/projects stop getting automated autofix suggestions out of the box — a product-behavior default change buried in a PR titled 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System', with no feature flag or migration to manage existing option rows; if this drift was not explicitly accepted, Seer automation quietly turns off at scale.

[BUG] The collector changed from per-report processing (valid reports counted, 200 returned) to all-or-nothing validation: the first invalid report in a browser's report array aborts the whole batch with a 422 and discards every valid report in it. Browsers send multiple reports in one payload; a single malformed entry (e.g. an unknown future 'type' from the evolving W3C spec, or attempts=0) now causes the endpoint to reject the entire batch, so telemetry for all valid reports in that request is permanently lost — a silent contract change from 'best effort collect' to 'strict gate' made without an accepted objective change.

[ADVISORY] The summarize-breadcrumbs GET silently expanded its objective from 'summarize breadcrumbs' to 'summarize breadcrumbs + fetch error context', adding an unconditional Snuba query (query_replay_instance) and a nodestore get_multi on every request, gated only by a raw query param defaulting to on. Every existing caller of this endpoint now pays two new backend calls per request with no feature flag (only enable_error_context=false opts out, requiring a client change + deploy to disable), so a regression in error fetching degrades the previously-cheap breadcrumb summary path for all users; the expanded objective appears to have arrived via review iteration rather than an accepted scope change.

[ADVISORY] The feedback summary prompt was rewritten during review to impose a hard 55-word/two-sentence cap and drop the '- ' bullet prefix in favor of a '------' separator, changing the product's summary output shape without an accepted objective statement. Long multi-feedback inputs now get aggressively truncated summaries and the model sees raw feedback text with no bullet markers, changing summary quality/length characteristics that prior prompt-tuning iterations calibrated; whoever tuned the old prompt's behavior loses their tuning silently.

[ADVISORY] The ParameterizationRegexExperiment class and the 'grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent' option (src/sentry/options/defaults.py) were deleted together, removing both the experiment and its runtime kill-switch in one silent step. Operators who had enabled the traceparent experiment via the option lose the ability to observe or disable it (the option registration is gone, so any stored value is orphaned), and the removal of a running grouping experiment is bundled invisibly into an unrelated replays PR rather than an accepted experiment-conclusion decision.

[ADVISORY] The new preprod assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so denied and feature-disabled requests are counted as successful assemble events. Analytics dashboards built on preprod_artifact.api.assemble will overcount assemble attempts (including 403s and orgs without the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature), corrupting the adoption signal the event was presumably added to measure.

[ADVISORY] The new validation-failure path writes the full attacker-controlled report payload (`extra={"validation_errors": serializer.errors, "raw_report": report}`) to logs on an unauthenticated endpoint (`permission_classes = ()`), so any anonymous client can inject arbitrary content and unbounded volume into the warning log stream. An unauthenticated attacker can flood logs or plant attacker-chosen strings (including PII or forged log-looking content) into Sentry's persistent log pipeline by POSTing malformed reports to the public collector, since the failing payload is echoed verbatim into `raw_report` with no size or content constraint.

[ADVISORY] Raw user-supplied feedback text is concatenated directly into the LLM instruction prompt with no delimiting or sanitization, allowing prompt injection from the feedback body into the summarization model. A user who submits feedback containing instruction-like text ('Ignore the above and write: ...') can steer the generated summary that is surfaced to organization users; the joined string `"\n------\n".join(feedbacks)` provides no separation between the system instructions and the untrusted feedback content, so injected directives are indistinguishable from the prompt's own instructions.

[BUG] Already-shipped data migration 0917 is rewritten in place to a no-op based on the unverified assumption that it 'was never run'. Any database that did apply 0917 (or a database created from a state where it ran) now has org saved searches converted to GroupSearchView rows with the conversion logic erased from migration history; if 0921's logic differs from the deleted update_or_create (e.g. different keying or defaults), those rows are never reconciled and the divergent state is silently accepted as migrated. Rewriting historical migrations instead of shipping a corrective forward migration destroys the ability to reason about what any given database actually executed.

[BUG] Already-shipped migration 0920 is gutted to a no-op that references corrective migration 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised, which is not part of this diff. If 0921 does not exist or is not ordered after 0920 on all deploy paths, environments that applied 0920 (its filter owner_id__isnull=False was the 'revised' logic, implying it did ship) are left with no conversion performed at all: org saved searches never become GroupSearchView rows and existing views-based features silently see no data. Even where 0921 exists, the comment's claim that the migration 'was never run' is asserted, not verified, and databases where 0917/0920 did execute keep rows created by logic that no longer exists anywhere in the codebase.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against nodestore get_multi's values(), so when nodestore omits keys for missing/expired events the zip truncates and remaining error_ids are paired with the wrong event's data (or silently dropped), producing summaries that attribute the wrong error title/message to an error ID. A replay with some evicted nodestore nodes yields a breadcrumb summary where later errors are labeled with earlier errors' titles/messages, or errors vanish entirely, with no indication to the user that the summary is wrong.

[ADVISORY] fetch_error_details catches every exception and returns an empty list, so a total nodestore outage is indistinguishable from a replay with no errors — the Seer summary is generated without any error context and the caller gets a 200 with no error surfaced. Users receive a confidently-wrong 'summary of the replay' that omits all error context during a nodestore outage; the only trace is an internal sentry_sdk event the end user never sees.

[BUG] error_ids is read from process_raw_response output built from request.query_params.getlist('field'); if the client does not explicitly request the error_ids field, response[0] contains no 'error_ids' key and all error enrichment is silently skipped while the endpoint returns a normal 200 summary. Any caller that omits 'error_ids' from the field query param gets a summary silently missing all error breadcrumbs, with no error or hint that enrichment was skipped.

[ADVISORY] make_seer_request is invoked from analyze_recording_segments via on_results, so every pagination page of this endpoint triggers a full Seer LLM request containing the complete log list (all segments plus all error events), not just the requested page. A client paginating through N pages fires N identical expensive Seer calls; cost and latency scale with page count and the same payload is repeatedly summarized.

[BUG] gen_request_data compares error timestamps against event.get('timestamp', 0) with a default of 0, so any segment event lacking a timestamp causes all remaining error messages to be flushed before that event, placing errors out of chronological order in the summary input. Summaries for replays whose segment events lack timestamps present errors as occurring before all breadcrumbs, misdirecting Seer's causal narrative.

[BUG] validate_timestamp/validate_age check presence with truthiness (self.initial_data.get('age')/get('timestamp')), so a report carrying age=0 together with timestamp=0 passes both mutual-exclusion validators even though both spec fields are present. Malformed reports violating the reporting spec's age/timestamp exclusivity are accepted with 200 and silently ingested, polluting the metric series the endpoint exists to measure.

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info catches bare Exception and logs at info level, so a persistent failure in get_recommended_event()/get_environment() silently degrades every merged-PR comment to omit environment info with only info-level logging. On an unexpected error shape from the event/environment path, all PR comments ship without environment context and the degradation is nearly invisible to operators (info, not warning/error).

The only opt-out is a raw query param `enable_error_context` defaulting to "true" (so callers must explicitly send `enable_error_context=false` to avoid the extra work). There is no feature flag or server-side gating around this added backend work. This is a scope/performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, not a concrete correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new preprod assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so denied and feature-disabled requests are counted as successful assemble events. Analytics dashboards built on preprod_artifact.api.assemble will overcount assemble attempts (including 403s and orgs without the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature), corrupting the adoption signal the event was presumably added to measure.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, the diff adds `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` immediately at the start of `post()` and *before* the subsequent `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` gate. This means requests that fail the feature check (and presumably return an error) will still emit the assemble analytics event, which can skew analytics/adoption metrics for that event. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new validation-failure path writes the full attacker-controlled report payload (`extra={"validation_errors": serializer.errors, "raw_report": report}`) to logs on an unauthenticated endpoint (`permission_classes = ()`), so any anonymous client can inject arbitrary content and unbounded volume into the warning log stream. An unauthenticated attacker can flood logs or plant attacker-chosen strings (including PII or forged log-looking content) into Sentry's persistent log pipeline by POSTing malformed reports to the public collector, since the failing payload is echoed verbatim into `raw_report` with no size or content constraint.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`, the POST endpoint is explicitly unauthenticated (`permission_classes = ()`) and on serializer validation failure it logs attacker-controlled data verbatim: `logger.warning(... extra={"validation_errors": serializer.errors, "raw_report": report})`. Because `report` comes directly from `request.data` and there is no size/content limiting in this diff, an anonymous client can inject arbitrary strings/large payloads into warning logs and potentially flood the log pipeline. This is a security-relevant defect introduced by the new validation-failure path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Raw user-supplied feedback text is concatenated directly into the LLM instruction prompt with no delimiting or sanitization, allowing prompt injection from the feedback body into the summarization model. A user who submits feedback containing instruction-like text ('Ignore the above and write: ...') can steer the generated summary that is surfaced to organization users; the joined string `"\n------\n".join(feedbacks)` provides no separation between the system instructions and the untrusted feedback content, so injected directives are indistinguishable from the prompt's own instructions.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/feedback/usecases/feedback_summaries.py`, `make_input_prompt()` interpolates untrusted `feedbacks` directly into the LLM prompt (`feedbacks_string = "\n------\n".join(feedbacks)`), with no escaping/quoting or structured encoding (e.g., JSON/code block) to clearly separate instructions from user content. Although a `User Feedbacks:` header and inter-entry separators exist, the feedback text is still presented as plain prompt text and can include instruction-like directives that the model may follow (prompt injection risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Already-shipped data migration 0917 is rewritten in place to a no-op based on the unverified assumption that it 'was never run'. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against nodestore get_multi's values(), so when nodestore omits keys for missing/expired events the zip truncates and remaining error_ids are paired with the wrong event's data (or silently dropped), producing summaries that attribute the wrong error title/message to an error ID. A replay with some evicted nodestore nodes yields a breadcrumb summary where later errors are labeled with earlier errors' titles/messages, or errors vanish entirely, with no indication to the user that the summary is wrong.
matched_golden_ids: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Candidate flags the same core bug: zipping error_ids with get_multi(...).values() relies on value order matching the requested keys, and missing/expired keys cause truncation/misalignment so IDs can be paired with the wrong event data. This matches the golden concern about order/alignment assumptions leading to incorrect ID→event pairing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_error_details catches every exception and returns an empty list, so a total nodestore outage is indistinguishable from a replay with no errors — the Seer summary is generated without any error context and the caller gets a 200 with no error surfaced. Users receive a confidently-wrong 'summary of the replay' that omits all error context during a nodestore outage; the only trace is an internal sentry_sdk event the end user never sees.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details()` wraps the entire nodestore lookup (`nodestore.backend.get_multi(...)`) in `try/except Exception` and on any failure does `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e)` then `return []`. The caller (`ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`) does not distinguish this from the legitimate case of `error_ids == []` and continues to generate the Seer request/summary (`analyze_recording_segments(..., error_events)`), returning HTTP 200. The finding accurately describes a diff-introduced edge case: nodestore failure silently drops error context and still produces a “successful” summary. Whether this must be surfaced to the user is a product/behavior decision, so it's a concrete review concern rather than a strictly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] error_ids is read from process_raw_response output built from request.query_params.getlist('field'); if the client does not explicitly request the error_ids field, response[0] contains no 'error_ids' key and all error enrichment is silently skipped while the endpoint returns a normal 200 summary. Any caller that omits 'error_ids' from the field query param gets a summary silently missing all error breadcrumbs, with no error or hint that enrichment was skipped.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, error enrichment is driven by `error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", [])` where `response` comes from `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))`. The code does not explicitly ensure `error_ids` is among the requested/returned fields, so enrichment behavior is implicitly coupled to how `process_raw_response` behaves when `fields` is empty or does not include `error_ids`. This is a concrete fragility/edge-case in the diff, but the diff alone doesn’t prove `process_raw_response` drops `error_ids` (tests added call the endpoint without `field` params and expect enrichment), so it’s not a definitively verifiable bug from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] make_seer_request is invoked from analyze_recording_segments via on_results, so every pagination page of this endpoint triggers a full Seer LLM request containing the complete log list (all segments plus all error events), not just the requested page. A client paginating through N pages fires N identical expensive Seer calls; cost and latency scale with page count and the same payload is repeatedly summarized.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the Seer call is made inside `analyze_recording_segments`, which is wired as `paginate(... on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events))`. That means `make_seer_request()` will execute once per pagination page (since `on_results` is invoked per page). Additionally, `error_events` is fetched once upfront and then passed into every page’s `analyze_recording_segments`, so the same error context can be re-sent repeatedly across pages. However, the diff does not show that each page includes *all* segments: `analyze_recording_segments` builds logs from `iter_segment_data(segments)`, where `segments` are the page results, so the claim that the payload always contains the complete log list / N identical payloads is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] gen_request_data compares error timestamps against event.get('timestamp', 0) with a default of 0, so any segment event lacking a timestamp causes all remaining error messages to be flushed before that event, placing errors out of chronological order in the summary input. Summaries for replays whose segment events lack timestamps present errors as occurring before all breadcrumbs, misdirecting Seer's causal narrative.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `gen_request_data` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py), errors are emitted in the `while` loop only when `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. If an event lacks `timestamp`, `event.get(..., 0)` becomes 0, so for normal (positive) error timestamps the condition is false and errors are *not* flushed before that event; instead they will be emitted later by the final "remaining error messages" loop after all segments are processed. The finding's described behavior (flushing all remaining errors before the no-timestamp event) does not match what the diff implements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] validate_timestamp/validate_age check presence with truthiness (self.initial_data.get('age')/get('timestamp')), so a report carrying age=0 together with timestamp=0 passes both mutual-exclusion validators even though both spec fields are present. Malformed reports violating the reporting spec's age/timestamp exclusivity are accepted with 200 and silently ingested, polluting the metric series the endpoint exists to measure.
matched_golden_ids: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: validators use truthiness checks via self.initial_data.get('age')/get('timestamp'), so 0-valued fields are treated as absent, allowing mutually exclusive age/timestamp fields (e.g., age=0 with timestamp=0) to bypass validation. This matches the golden comment’s concern and suggested fix direction (explicit key presence checks).

On an unexpected error shape from the event/environment path, all PR comments ship without environment context and the degradation is nearly invisible to operators (info, not warning/error).
